model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the mean effect sizes, with error bars indicating variability, for six different multilingual BERT models—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across eight linguistic categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” is scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis lists the linguistic categories in alphabetical order from left to right. Each category contains a group of six bars, each representing one model variant, color-coded as follows: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The bars are arranged in a grouped format, with each group corresponding to a linguistic category. The height of each bar indicates the mean effect size for that model within that linguistic group, and the error bars extend above and below the bar to show the standard deviation or confidence interval. For example, in the IE-Indic category, the tallest bar is mBERT-R₂ (light green), reaching approximately 20, while the shortest bar is mBERT-L₂ (light blue), at approximately 2. In the Semitic category, the tallest bar is XLM-B₂ (dark red), reaching approximately 20, and the shortest is mBERT-R₂ (dark green), at approximately -2. The bars are not sorted by height; they appear in the order specified by the legend, which is also the order of the models listed in the legend box on the right. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlines beyond the standard color coding and error bars.
